::: {.callout-important title="Review baseline"}
This architecture description was checked against exported VBA at commit
`8cfa4a786f1969a86c461908c66ceb37d821d96c`. It describes static source
observations, not a completed runtime, security, accessibility, or regulatory
assessment. Deployment-specific settings and production data were not inspected.
:::

## Purpose and method

This page explains the current NADABAS system boundary, major components,
runtime state, data flows, and trust boundaries. It is informed by
[ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010:2022](https://www.iso.org/standard/74393.html) and uses the
context, container, and dynamic-view ideas of the [C4
model](https://c4model.com/diagrams). It does not claim conformance to either.

Architecture statements use stable claim identifiers. The corresponding source
links and review status are recorded in the [architecture evidence
register](architecture-evidence.qmd).

### Evidence status

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Source-verified** | Directly supported by the exported source at the baseline commit. Runtime behaviour may still require testing. |
| **Environment-dependent** | The source supports the behaviour, but configuration or infrastructure determines the result. |
| **Legacy-draft** | Present in the earlier technical draft but not yet verified in source or a supported environment. |
| **Unknown** | Evidence is incomplete; the statement must not be treated as established behaviour. |

## Stakeholders and concerns

| Stakeholder or reviewer | Primary concerns |
|---|---|
| National accounts user | Correct workbook data, understandable messages, recoverable operations, and predictable load/save behaviour. |
| NADABAS maintainer | Traceability from documentation to exported VBA, maintainability, testability, and controlled migration seams. |
| Database administrator | Supported database engine, connection lifecycle, permissions, concurrency, backup, restore, and schema compatibility. |
| Security and privacy reviewer | Credential handling, trust boundaries, logging, least privilege, data classification, and external integrations. |
| Operations reviewer | Installation prerequisites, registry configuration, diagnostics, recovery, and version compatibility. |
| Accessibility and localization reviewer | Plain English, language metadata, translatable terminology, text alternatives, and right-to-left readiness. |
| Release maintainer | Reproducible source export/import, signing, versioning, CI evidence, and release provenance. |

## System context

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  user["National accounts user"]
  maintainer["NADABAS administrator or maintainer"]
  excel["NADABAS in Microsoft Excel"]
  database[("Configured database")]
  registry[("Windows user registry")]
  files[("Local or shared file storage")]

  user -->|"Uses ribbon, forms, and workbooks"| excel
  maintainer -->|"Configures databases and administers content"| excel
  excel -->|"Reads and writes statistical and system data"| database
  excel -->|"Reads and writes local settings"| registry
  excel -->|"Opens, saves, imports, and exports files"| files
```

**Diagram description.** Users operate NADABAS inside Microsoft Excel. The
add-in connects Excel workbooks to a configured database, reads local settings
from the Windows registry, and interacts with local or shared files. These
external stores are separate trust and operational boundaries.

**ARCH-001 — Source-verified.** NADABAS is an Excel/VBA add-in whose user-facing
entry points include the ribbon, forms, and Excel application events.

**ARCH-002 — Source-verified.** Database configuration is loaded from the
Windows user registry when the add-in starts. Configuration can include a
database type, server or file location, catalog, user name, and password.

**ARCH-003 — Source-verified.** The source models a base database, an exchange
database, and optional satellite databases. A deployment does not necessarily
use every role.

## Internal component view

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
  subgraph host["Microsoft Excel process"]
    workbook["Registered workbook\nNamed ranges and cell data"]
    subgraph addin["NADABAS VBA add-in"]
      ui["Ribbon and UserForms\nCommands and feedback"]
      events["Application events\nWorkbook lifecycle"]
      orchestration["Workflow modules\nLoad, save, batch, administration"]
      state["Session state\nGlobals and domain classes"]
      data["Data access\nclsDB, DBInterface, schema modules"]
    end
  end
  registry[("Windows registry")]
  base[("Base database")]
  exchange[("Exchange database")]
  satellite[("Optional satellite database")]
  files[("File system")]

  ui --> orchestration
  events --> orchestration
  workbook <--> orchestration
  orchestration <--> state
  orchestration --> data
  state --> data
  data <--> base
  data <--> exchange
  data <--> satellite
  orchestration <--> files
  state <--> registry
```

**Diagram description.** The ribbon, forms, and application events start VBA
workflows. Workflow modules inspect workbook named ranges, coordinate global and
object state, and use a shared ADO-based data access layer. Database roles,
registry settings, and files sit outside the add-in boundary.

| Component | Responsibility | Primary evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Startup and shutdown | Initializes language, Excel application events, session objects, and database settings. Shutdown cleanup is currently a placeholder. | `AutoOpenClose.bas` |
| Ribbon and forms | Expose commands, show status, and invalidate controls when session or workbook state changes. | `RibbonUI.bas`, files below `vba/forms/` |
| Application events | Observe workbook open, activation, changes, save, and close events; coordinate registered workbook behaviour. | `AppEvents.cls` |
| Session and domain state | Hold active database roles, user settings, workbook state, classifications, correspondences, permissions, and other collections. | `Globals.bas`, `clsDB.cls`, related classes |
| Workflow modules | Validate definitions and coordinate load, save, batch, document, classification, and administration operations. | Command modules below `vba/modules/` |
| Data access | Build connection strings, open ADO connections and recordsets, execute SQL, and create database objects. | `cmdOpen_Close_Database.bas`, `DBInterface.bas`, `DbCreateTables.bas` |

## Database roles and deployment variants

**ARCH-004 — Source-verified.** `clsDB` defines SQL Server/SQL Express and
Microsoft Access `.accdb` database types. Legacy `.mdb` is retained as an enum
value but is explicitly rejected when opening a database.

| Role | Source responsibility | Review note |
|---|---|---|
| Base database | Default database for workbook data and system metadata. | Confirm supported database products and versions for each deployment. |
| Exchange database | Temporary current database for import and export workflows. | Confirm governance, transport, retention, and access controls locally. |
| Satellite database | Optional database linked to a base database through registry configuration. | Confirm whether it is supported and used in the reviewed environment. |

SQL Server connections may use integrated Windows security or supplied
credentials, depending on configuration. Access connections use the configured
Microsoft ACE OLE DB provider and a database file path. These are
environment-dependent behaviours and must be verified without copying secrets
into documentation or review evidence.

## Runtime state and connection lifecycle

```{mermaid}
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> Starting
  Starting --> Sleeping: "Initialize events and settings"
  Sleeping --> DatabaseSelected: "User selects a configured database"
  DatabaseSelected --> Active: "Connection and initialization succeed"
  DatabaseSelected --> Sleeping: "Selection or connection fails"
  Active --> Operation: "Load, save, import, export, or administration"
  Operation --> Active: "Close operation-level connection"
  Active --> Sleeping: "Close database"
```

**Diagram description.** Startup creates the session in a sleeping state. A
successful database selection and initialization activates NADABAS. Individual
workflows open and close database resources around their work. Failure returns
the session to a sleeping state.

**ARCH-005 — Source-verified.** Startup registers an `AppEvents` instance with
the Excel `Application`, initializes base and exchange database objects, marks
NADABAS as sleeping, and loads registry-backed database settings.

**ARCH-006 — Source-verified.** Opening a database constructs a connection for
the selected database type, tests or initializes required structures, loads
user settings and workbook metadata, and returns the application to sleeping
state when connection or initialization fails.

**ARCH-007 — Source-verified.** `auto_close` contains no cleanup implementation.
Any assumption that application shutdown releases or persists additional state
beyond object teardown by Excel is therefore **unknown** until runtime-tested.

## Principal data flows

### Load or import

```{mermaid}
sequenceDiagram
  actor User
  participant UI as "Ribbon or batch workflow"
  participant Loader as "Load workflow"
  participant WB as "Excel workbook"
  participant DB as "Current database"

  User->>UI: Start load or import
  UI->>Loader: Select base or exchange database
  Loader->>WB: Read definitions and named ranges
  Loader->>Loader: Validate definitions and year selection
  Loader->>DB: Open connection and query data
  DB-->>Loader: Values and metadata
  Loader->>WB: Update target cells and source information
  Loader->>DB: Record last-get metadata when applicable
  Loader->>DB: Close connection
  Loader-->>User: Show statistics, missing values, or errors
```

**ARCH-008 — Source-verified.** Load/import validates workbook definitions,
opens the selected database, scans `DBLinks` or `ExchLinks`, updates workbook
areas, records metadata where applicable, and closes the connection.

### Save or export

```{mermaid}
sequenceDiagram
  actor User
  participant UI as "Ribbon or batch workflow"
  participant Saver as "Save workflow"
  participant WB as "Excel workbook"
  participant DB as "Current database"

  User->>UI: Start save or export
  UI->>Saver: Select base or exchange database
  Saver->>WB: Read definitions, year, and data areas
  Saver->>Saver: Validate definitions and conflicts
  Saver->>DB: Open connection and write values
  Saver->>DB: Update workbook metadata
  Saver->>DB: Close connection
  Saver->>WB: Optionally save workbook and clear dirty state
  Saver-->>User: Show statistics or errors
```

**ARCH-009 — Source-verified.** Save/export validates definitions, writes
workbook data through the shared data-access routines, updates workbook state,
and closes the connection. The exact transaction and concurrency guarantees are
not yet documented and require database-specific verification.

## Trust boundaries and security-sensitive interfaces

| Boundary or interface | Data or capability crossing it | Required review |
|---|---|---|
| Excel workbook to add-in | Named ranges, formulas, cell values, workbook paths, and events. | Validate untrusted or malformed workbook behaviour and macro-signing expectations. |
| Add-in to database | Statistical data, system metadata, SQL commands, identities, and permissions. | Review least privilege, parameterization, transaction boundaries, logging, and recovery. |
| Add-in to Windows registry | Language, provider, database location, user name, and potentially a password. | Treat registry credential storage as a security finding to assess and migrate; never publish values. |
| Add-in to file system and shell | Workbook and document paths, file operations, and opening files or URLs. | Validate paths, file types, external destinations, and user confirmation. |
| Add-in to Windows/Office APIs | Excel events, ADO/ADOX, WMI, and shell integration. | Document supported Windows, Office, drivers, trust settings, and failure behaviour. |

::: {.callout-warning title="Credential handling requires a decision"}
The current source can save database credentials in the Windows user registry.
This page records that observation; it does not approve the design. Each
deployment must determine whether credentials are used, how the registry is
protected, and what replacement mechanism is required. Track the target design
in an ADR and a security issue.
:::

## Quality concerns and known unknowns

| Concern | Current evidence | Next verification |
|---|---|---|
| Functional correctness | Main entry points and static flows are traceable in source. | Exercise supported Excel, Access, and SQL Server scenarios with representative non-production workbooks. |
| Availability and recovery | Connection failures generally return NADABAS to sleeping state and show messages. | Test interrupted reads/writes, database outages, Excel termination, and recovery steps. |
| Data integrity | VBA performs definition checks and records workbook metadata. | Document transaction scope, constraints, conflict handling, and authoritative reconciliation procedures. |
| Security and privacy | Trust boundaries and sensitive configuration paths are identifiable. | Complete threat modelling, credential migration, log review, least-privilege testing, and data classification. |
| Accessibility and localization | Quarto output declares English; the interface loads language resources. | Test keyboard use, screen readers, translated UI strings, text expansion, Unicode, and right-to-left presentation. |
| Portability | The solution depends on desktop Excel, VBA, Windows APIs, ADO/ADOX, and database drivers. | Record supported versions and define seams for optional .NET components without changing verified behaviour. |

## International review

Use the [international review and localization guide](../development/international-review.qmd)
to prepare a review package. Reviewers should comment against claim IDs and
state the deployment, jurisdiction, language, and reviewer role they assessed.

This architecture is a common technical baseline. It does not by itself
demonstrate acceptance by the African Union, European Union, ASEAN, their member
states, or any national authority.

## Maintenance rule

Update this page and the evidence register in the same pull request when a
change affects a documented component, trust boundary, database role, or data
flow. Record consequential decisions as a small [architecture decision
record](../decisions/index.qmd). Do not silently convert an environment-dependent
or unknown statement into a verified claim.
